Speaker 1 started transcription
HR
Hartwell, Rena
12 seconds0:12
Hartwell, Rena 12 seconds
Okay, let's start. Two things today. First, the claims-data vendor for next year: renew Meridian or move to Lumen. Second, who owns the data quality checks after cutover. I want a direction on the first before we leave.

DO
Osei, Daniel
35 seconds0:35
Osei, Daniel 35 seconds
Quick context. Meridian renewal is $410k for the year, same as now. Lumen came in at $355k but that is the first year only, and the integration work is on us.

LP
Pereira, Lucia
58 seconds0:58
Pereira, Lucia 58 seconds
I'd renew Meridian. We know it, the finance team's reports are built on its field names, and I do not want to rebuild those in Q1.

KB
Brandt, Kiran
1 minute 20 seconds1:20
Brandt, Kiran 1 minute 20 seconds
I lean Lumen. Their refresh is daily and Meridian's is weekly. That is the whole reason we are having this conversation.

SN
Nakamura, Sam
1 minute 35 seconds1:35
Nakamura, Sam 1 minute 35 seconds
Yeah.

HR
Hartwell, Rena
1 minute 44 seconds1:44
Hartwell, Rena 1 minute 44 seconds
Sam, anything from you?

SN
Nakamura, Sam
1 minute 50 seconds1:50
Nakamura, Sam 1 minute 50 seconds
Not yet. I want to see the field mapping first.

AV
Varga, Anika
2 minutes 11 seconds2:11
Varga, Anika 2 minutes 11 seconds
Can I add a third option? We could renew Meridian for six months only and run Lumen in parallel on one region. Then we decide with real numbers.

DO
Osei, Daniel
2 minutes 30 seconds2:30
Osei, Daniel 2 minutes 30 seconds
That costs more in the short term. Roughly $205k for the half year plus a Lumen pilot, call it $60k. So about $265k before we choose anything.

LP
Pereira, Lucia
2 minutes 52 seconds2:52
Pereira, Lucia 2 minutes 52 seconds
I can live with the six-month renewal if the Lumen pilot stays on one region and does not touch the finance reports.

KB
Brandt, Kiran
3 minutes 10 seconds3:10
Brandt, Kiran 3 minutes 10 seconds
A pilot is fine but it delays the daily refresh by half a year. I'd still rather go straight to Lumen.

HR
Hartwell, Rena
3 minutes 32 seconds3:32
Hartwell, Rena 3 minutes 32 seconds
Kiran, if the pilot showed the refresh fixed the lag, would that be enough for you?

KB
Brandt, Kiran
3 minutes 46 seconds3:46
Brandt, Kiran 3 minutes 46 seconds
If it shows the lag is gone on real claims, yes. Then I'd drop my objection.

DO
Osei, Daniel
4 minutes 5 seconds4:05
Osei, Daniel 4 minutes 5 seconds
One correction on my number. The Lumen pilot is $75k, not $60k. I had the old quote.

AV
Varga, Anika
4 minutes 22 seconds4:22
Varga, Anika 4 minutes 22 seconds
That makes the six-month path about $280k. Still under a full year of Meridian.

HR
Hartwell, Rena
4 minutes 40 seconds4:40
Hartwell, Rena 4 minutes 40 seconds
Right. Let me move to the second item and come back.

LP
Pereira, Lucia
4 minutes 55 seconds4:55
Pereira, Lucia 4 minutes 55 seconds
Before that, who is the pilot region? Whoever picks it decides how fair the comparison is.

SN
Nakamura, Sam
5 minutes 12 seconds5:12
Nakamura, Sam 5 minutes 12 seconds
I would pick the Midwest. It has the messiest provider data, so it is the hardest test.

LP
Pereira, Lucia
5 minutes 30 seconds5:30
Pereira, Lucia 5 minutes 30 seconds
Midwest is also where the finance team does the most reporting. That is exactly what I said I did not want to touch.

SN
Nakamura, Sam
5 minutes 48 seconds5:48
Nakamura, Sam 5 minutes 48 seconds
Then the Southeast. Smaller, and finance barely uses it.

HR
Hartwell, Rena
6 minutes 2 seconds6:02
Hartwell, Rena 6 minutes 2 seconds
Southeast works for me. Anika, can you confirm with Lumen that they can start there?

AV
Varga, Anika
6 minutes 15 seconds6:15
Varga, Anika 6 minutes 15 seconds
I will ask them this week and tell the group by Friday.

HR
Hartwell, Rena
6 minutes 35 seconds6:35
Hartwell, Rena 6 minutes 35 seconds
Okay. On data quality checks. Daniel, your team runs them today.

DO
Osei, Daniel
6 minutes 50 seconds6:50
Osei, Daniel 6 minutes 50 seconds
We do, but only because nobody else would. If Lumen comes in, the checks have to move closer to the data owners. I do not want to carry them after cutover.

KB
Brandt, Kiran
7 minutes 12 seconds7:12
Brandt, Kiran 7 minutes 12 seconds
My team could take them, but only if we get the two analyst headcount we asked for in the budget. Without that, no.

HR
Hartwell, Rena
7 minutes 30 seconds7:30
Hartwell, Rena 7 minutes 30 seconds
The headcount is not decided. That goes to the budget review on the 28th.

LP
Pereira, Lucia
7 minutes 48 seconds7:48
Pereira, Lucia 7 minutes 48 seconds
I don't think the checks belong with Kiran at all. They should sit with Sam's group, since Sam owns the provider master.

SN
Nakamura, Sam
8 minutes 5 seconds8:05
Nakamura, Sam 8 minutes 5 seconds
I can't take that on right now. My team is already behind on the master clean-up.

AV
Varga, Anika
8 minutes 22 seconds8:22
Varga, Anika 8 minutes 22 seconds
Could we split it? Kiran's team takes the claims checks and Sam's takes the provider checks.

KB
Brandt, Kiran
8 minutes 38 seconds8:38
Brandt, Kiran 8 minutes 38 seconds
A split I could do, still subject to the headcount.

SN
Nakamura, Sam
8 minutes 50 seconds8:50
Nakamura, Sam 8 minutes 50 seconds
A split I could do too, but later, not before March.

HR
Hartwell, Rena
9 minutes 8 seconds9:08
Hartwell, Rena 9 minutes 8 seconds
So for the checks nothing is settled. Daniel keeps them until at least March. Let me write that down.

DO
Osei, Daniel
9 minutes 25 seconds9:25
Osei, Daniel 9 minutes 25 seconds
Fine, as long as it says until March and not forever.

HR
Hartwell, Rena
9 minutes 42 seconds9:42
Hartwell, Rena 9 minutes 42 seconds
Back to the vendor. Here is where I land. We renew Meridian for six months, we run the Lumen pilot in the Southeast, and we decide in the spring. Any objection?

LP
Pereira, Lucia
10 minutes 0 seconds10:00
Pereira, Lucia 10 minutes 0 seconds
No objection from me.

KB
Brandt, Kiran
10 minutes 6 seconds10:06
Brandt, Kiran 10 minutes 6 seconds
I'll go along with that.

SN
Nakamura, Sam
10 minutes 12 seconds10:12
Nakamura, Sam 10 minutes 12 seconds
Okay.

DO
Osei, Daniel
10 minutes 20 seconds10:20
Osei, Daniel 10 minutes 20 seconds
I will draft the six-month renewal terms. One caution: Meridian may ask for a price increase on a short term. I have seen that before.

HR
Hartwell, Rena
10 minutes 42 seconds10:42
Hartwell, Rena 10 minutes 42 seconds
If they ask for more than ten percent, come back to me before agreeing.

AV
Varga, Anika
10 minutes 58 seconds10:58
Varga, Anika 10 minutes 58 seconds
I will also write down the pilot success measures, refresh lag and match rate, so we are not arguing about it in the spring.

HR
Hartwell, Rena
11 minutes 16 seconds11:16
Hartwell, Rena 11 minutes 16 seconds
Good. Please send those to the group by the 25th.

LP
Pereira, Lucia
11 minutes 30 seconds11:30
Pereira, Lucia 11 minutes 30 seconds
One more thing. Please do not share the Meridian pricing outside this group. Procurement has not seen it yet.

HR
Hartwell, Rena
11 minutes 44 seconds11:44
Hartwell, Rena 11 minutes 44 seconds
Understood. That stays in this room. Thanks everyone.

result.summary:
Decision announced by Rena Hartwell: Run Lumen pilot in the Southeast. 2 open questions, 6 open blockers, 5 people took an explicit position on an option.

## The main point

Rena Hartwell announced the vendor decision: renew Meridian for six months, run a Lumen pilot in the Southeast, and decide on the full vendor switch in the spring. After the announcement, Lucia Pereira said "No objection from me" and Kiran Brandt said "I'll go along with that." The data quality checks question is unresolved; Rena's interim ruling is that Daniel Osei's team keeps them until at least March. Who owns them after March depends partly on a headcount decision going to budget review on the 28th, and no agreement on permanent ownership was reached. Daniel will draft the six-month Meridian renewal terms but warned Meridian may seek a price increase on a short-term deal.

## Presented, no challenge recorded

- Daniel Osei (confirmed by Rena Hartwell): Daniel's team currently runs the data quality checks only because no one else took them on.
- Rena Hartwell: The final vendor choice is deferred to spring.

## Open questions

- Rena Hartwell raised: Which claims-data vendor to use next year — renew Meridian or move to Lumen.
- Rena Hartwell raised: Who owns the data quality checks after cutover.

## Where people stand

- Lucia Pereira: wants to renew Meridian, citing the finance team's reports being built on its field names and not wanting to rebuild them in Q1; accepted the six-month renewal provided the Lumen pilot stays on one region and does not touch the finance reports; objected to the Midwest as pilot region because finance does the most reporting there; opposes the checks sitting with Kiran's team, saying "I don't think the checks belong with Kiran at all — they should sit with Sam's group."
- Kiran Brandt: wants to go straight to Lumen for its daily refresh; accepted the pilot as a path forward if it shows "the lag is gone on real claims"; agreed to take the claims-side data quality checks subject to "the two analyst headcount we asked for in the budget — without that, no"; accepted a split with Sam's team on the same condition.
- Anika Varga: proposed the six-month Meridian renewal with a one-region Lumen pilot "to decide with real numbers"; updated the cost to roughly $280k after Daniel corrected the pilot quote; proposed splitting the checks between Kiran's team for claims and Sam's for provider checks.
- Sam Nakamura: proposed the Southeast as pilot region as "smaller, and finance barely uses it"; said he cannot take on the data quality checks now because his team "is already behind on the master clean-up"; accepted a split with Kiran's team "but later, not before March."
- Daniel Osei said "I do not want to carry them after cutover" and "as long as it says until March and not forever."

## What is blocking progress

- Sam Nakamura has not yet reviewed the field mapping between Meridian and Lumen, which he said he needs before taking a position on the vendor question.
- Whether Meridian will seek a price increase on a short-term renewal is unknown; Daniel Osei flagged this and said he has seen it before.
- The two analyst headcount positions Kiran Brandt's team requested have not been approved; decision goes to budget review on the 28th.
- Permanent ownership of the data quality checks after March is unresolved.
- Anika Varga has not yet confirmed with Lumen whether they can start the pilot in the Southeast.
- Procurement has not yet reviewed the Meridian pricing (raised by Lucia Pereira).

## Next steps

- Rena Hartwell asked Anika Varga to confirm with Lumen that they can start the pilot in the Southeast.
- Anika Varga will ask Lumen this week and tell the group by Friday.
- Daniel Osei will draft the six-month Meridian renewal terms.
- Anika Varga will document pilot success measures (refresh lag and match rate) and send them to the group by the 25th.

## Awaiting a reply

- Rena Hartwell asked Anika Varga to confirm with Lumen that they can start in the Southeast; Anika Varga said she will respond by Friday, no confirmation recorded yet.

## Things people asserted that others may want to check

- Daniel Osei said Lumen's quote of $355k applies to the first year only.
- Daniel Osei said Meridian's full-year renewal is $410k, same as current spend.
- Kiran Brandt said Lumen's data refresh is daily while Meridian's is weekly, and that this difference is the reason the vendor decision is being discussed.
- Anika Varga said the six-month Meridian renewal plus the corrected $75k Lumen pilot totals about $280k.

## Marked private

- Marked private by Lucia Pereira: Meridian pricing is not to be shared outside this group; procurement has not yet seen it. Rena Hartwell confirmed it stays in the room.
